patch_description:
This design keeps the low-lag endpoint-regression insight from the stronger prior programs, but replaces the expensive per-window Kalman/IRLS pipeline with a multiscale robust trend-consensus tracker.

Two robust causal local-linear regressions are computed at different horizons: a short horizon detects legitimate acceleration early, while a longer horizon rejects short-lived noise. Their slope agreement controls the endpoint measurement and adaptive tracker gain. The sequential tracker then uses a bounded velocity-consensus update: its velocity moves toward a blend of the multiscale local slope and the actual filtered step, with acceleration limited by local residual noise. A directional confirmation gate suppresses weak opposite-direction movements without blocking strong, sustained real reversals. This directly targets the observed tradeoff between the highly responsive but reversal-heavy Kalman variants and the smoother but laggier local-trend variants.

The implementation is vectorized for window feature extraction and has only one lightweight streaming loop, substantially reducing latency relative to repeated per-window iterative regression.
